text: Every morning, I wake up at six thirty. I don't jump out of bed right away. First, I open the window and take a deep breath of fresh air. Then I drink a big glass of water. After that, I make my bed. It only takes one minute, but it makes my room look clean and calm. Next, I take a quick shower and get dressed. For breakfast, I usually eat toast with eggs and a banana. I also make a cup of coffee, but I drink it slowly. While I eat, I write three things I want to do that day in a small notebook. This helps me stay focused. I don't check my phone until I finish breakfast. Before I leave the house, I look in the mirror and smile. It sounds a little silly, but it really helps me start the day in a good mood.

Last Monday, I missed my bus to work. I saw it leave just as I got to the bus stop. The next bus was in thirty minutes, and I didn't want to be late. Then I noticed the city bikes near the corner. I had never used one before, but I decided to try. I downloaded the app, paid two dollars, and unlocked a blue bike. At first, I felt a little nervous because there were many cars on the street. But soon I found a quiet bike lane next to the park. The air was cool, and the trees looked beautiful. I arrived at the office ten minutes early! My coworkers were surprised when I told them how I got there. Now I ride a bike to work two or three times a week. Missing that bus was the best mistake I made all year.

Ana's grandmother makes the best chicken soup in the family. Every winter, everyone asks for it. This year, Ana wanted to learn the recipe, so she visited her grandmother on Sunday morning. They started by washing the vegetables: carrots, potatoes, onions, and a little celery. Ana cut them into small pieces while her grandmother put the chicken in a big pot of water. “Don't rush,” her grandmother said. “Good soup needs time.” They let it cook slowly for almost two hours. While they waited, they drank tea and looked at old family photos. Ana heard stories she had never heard before. Finally, her grandmother added salt, pepper, and fresh herbs. The kitchen smelled wonderful. Ana tasted the soup and smiled. It was perfect. Now she has the recipe written on a small card, but she knows the most important part was the time they spent together.

When I turned thirty-five, I decided to learn something new. I bought a cheap guitar and started watching free lessons online. The first week was hard. My fingers hurt, and every song sounded terrible. My neighbor even knocked on the wall once! I almost gave up. But my friend Leo told me, “Practice a little every day, not a lot one day.” So I changed my plan. Now I practice for just fifteen minutes after dinner. I play slowly and repeat the same chords again and again. After two months, something changed. I could play my first full song from beginning to end. It wasn't perfect, but I was very proud. Last weekend, I played it at a small family party, and everyone sang along. I'm still a beginner, but I learned that small steps can take you far.
